sourceEvidence.label: Current RAGFlow lab deployment configuration and role bootstrap

assessment.summary: Per-dependency networks with external stateful port/direction policy and restricted egress fit the current local lab; separating roles adds a stronger parser/API/admin boundary. Nothing applied.

nonNegotiables: Preserve named volumes and existing data
Do not change image/release in the segmentation migration
assumptions: No latency or RSS budget supplied
Current deployment is rootless Podman6.1.4 / Netavark2.1.0
Strict isolation and bridge/inet enforcement must be validated in the correct namespace
No new listener or candidate firewall policy was applied

opportunities.title: Limit inter-service and external network authority
opportunities.summary: Make client source/destination/port relationships explicit and restrict excess, reverse and egress flows.
opportunities.diagnosis: Shared L2 exposes dependency peers and RAGFlow listeners; monolith combines network/secret authority across API, admin and ingestion.

evidence.claim: All seven services share backend; only RAGFlow also has outbound.
App client ports are configured; active ss confirms MySQL, ES, MinIO, Kvrocks6379 and NATS. CH9000 is configured but not captured as established.
nginx/API/admin/ingestor run together; actual admin9381 listens wildcard.
API and ingestor heartbeat uses POST /api/v1/admin/reports at admin9381.
Previous scoped runtime validation observed beta MCP private metadata disclosure internally; nginx blocks MCP.
Previous scoped runtime validation observed API original document read after deactivation via nginx.
RCE of the multihomed RAGFlow monolith retains its legitimate database credentials and client-port access.

desiredInvariants: Dependencies accept new flows only from authorized clients on required ports
Dependencies do not initiate new flows to peers or RAGFlow management listeners
Established/related replies are allowed without opening all ephemeral ports
Model/DNS egress has an explicit allowlist and no direct bypass
Policy owner is outside workload namespaces
Policy applies before readiness and survives recreate/reboot
IPv6, DNS and host gateway paths are covered

options.title: Option 1: Shared backend with external stateful ACL
options.summary: Keep shared L2, enforce client pairs/ports and restricted egress externally.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Topology and/or port policy narrow peer reachability; lifecycle enforcement tests remain required.
Exact allowed destination ports and reverse-flow tests required.
Only separate role configs/credentials can reduce same-container authority.
Role split needs a reports-only relay or a verified intentional change to telemetry; TCP alone cannot distinguish paths.
Beta authorization scope must be fixed separately; retain current MCP gateway block.
Deactivate-account credential checking/revocation must be fixed separately.

tradeoffs.assessment: Blocks extra paths while enforcement works, but loss of policy restores shared adjacency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test each denied source/destination/port against a controlled listening fixture, including reverse NEW and lifecycle recreation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Rules and conntrack add packet-processing work; no application proxy hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare p50/p95 retrieval latency, ingestion throughput and CPU with identical corpus/model/hardware; agree budget after baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: Conntrack and policy entries; total effect not measured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak cgroup memory/RSS, socket/conntrack counts and restart behavior against baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: One wrong policy can affect the whole segment; filter availability must gate workloads.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise policy failure, container/network recreate and VM restart; prove fail-closed readiness and allowed workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Namespace-aware L2 policy and lifecycle controller; no new network names.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse diagnostic runbook, identity updates, counters/logs, owned-rule rollback and DNS failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Keep current memberships; add only owned policy objects, with rollback.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Synthetic login/upload/ingest/retrieve/delete and preserved data/volumes; inspect actual memberships and replay rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: Versioned connection matrix must accompany new services or ports; role separation adds ownership review.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require explicit new-connection declaration and negative policy tests when adding a dependency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Same image and named-volume format permit reverting configuration; previous exposure returns on rollback.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Restore original memberships and remove only own policy tables; do not delete data volumes.

residualRisks: RAGFlow monolith retains all allowed data authority

affectedComponents: network/policy lifecycle integration in dedicated Podman VM
RAGFlow role configs for role-separation option

options.title: Option 2: Per-dependency networks plus stateful ACL and constrained egress
options.summary: Six internal pair networks, exact client-port policy, and approved model/DNS egress.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Topology and/or port policy narrow peer reachability; lifecycle enforcement tests remain required.
Exact allowed destination ports and reverse-flow tests required.
Only separate role configs/credentials can reduce same-container authority.
Role split needs a reports-only relay or a verified intentional change to telemetry; TCP alone cannot distinguish paths.
Beta authorization scope must be fixed separately; retain current MCP gateway block.
Deactivate-account credential checking/revocation must be fixed separately.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes direct dependency adjacency and blocks excess/reverse NEW flows if topology and external enforcement pass validation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test each denied source/destination/port against a controlled listening fixture, including reverse NEW and lifecycle recreation.

tradeoffs.assessment: More interfaces and rules, no new application proxy hop; latency unknown.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare p50/p95 retrieval latency, ingestion throughput and CPU with identical corpus/model/hardware; agree budget after baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: Additional bridge/veth/IPAM and conntrack entries; memory not measured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak cgroup memory/RSS, socket/conntrack counts and restart behavior against baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: Per-service topology improves readability; controller, DNS and stable identity become availability dependencies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise policy failure, container/network recreate and VM restart; prove fail-closed readiness and allowed workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Six explicit networks plus IPAM/DNS/policy ownership, readiness gate and recreate handling.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse diagnostic runbook, identity updates, counters/logs, owned-rule rollback and DNS failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Replace all old backend memberships, preserve aliases/volumes/images, keep rollback to original Compose.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Synthetic login/upload/ingest/retrieve/delete and preserved data/volumes; inspect actual memberships and replay rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: Versioned connection matrix must accompany new services or ports; role separation adds ownership review.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require explicit new-connection declaration and negative policy tests when adding a dependency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Same image and named-volume format permit reverting configuration; previous exposure returns on rollback.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Restore original memberships and remove only own policy tables; do not delete data volumes.

residualRisks: RAGFlow is multihomed with all permitted client access
Authorized database operations remain usable after RCE
Rootless filtering and strict isolation must be proven
Same-container API/admin/ingestor share secrets and localhost

options.title: Option 3: Separate gateway, API, admin and ingestion roles
options.summary: Split roles and credentials with pair networks, data-plane policy, management gateway and reports-only heartbeat relay.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Topology and/or port policy narrow peer reachability; lifecycle enforcement tests remain required.
Exact allowed destination ports and reverse-flow tests required.
Only separate role configs/credentials can reduce same-container authority.
Role split needs a reports-only relay or a verified intentional change to telemetry; TCP alone cannot distinguish paths.
Beta authorization scope must be fixed separately; retain current MCP gateway block.
Deactivate-account credential checking/revocation must be fixed separately.

tradeoffs.assessment: Separates parser/API/admin authority if actual client/secret sets are narrowed; retains authorization bugs on allowed paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test each denied source/destination/port against a controlled listening fixture, including reverse NEW and lifecycle recreation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Gateway and heartbeat relay add hops; role boundaries and connection pools require measurement.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare p50/p95 retrieval latency, ingestion throughput and CPU with identical corpus/model/hardware; agree budget after baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: Additional processes, native resources and client pools; cannot multiply existing 6GiB limit as if free.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak cgroup memory/RSS, socket/conntrack counts and restart behavior against baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: Independent role restarts and fault boundaries, but more readiness, migration and relay dependencies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise policy failure, container/network recreate and VM restart; prove fail-closed readiness and allowed workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Separate configs/keys, one migration owner, role policy, management gateway and heartbeat relay.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse diagnostic runbook, identity updates, counters/logs, owned-rule rollback and DNS failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Audit role bootstrap/client dependencies; split startup/config without changing image/volume schema; rollback to monolith.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Synthetic login/upload/ingest/retrieve/delete and preserved data/volumes; inspect actual memberships and replay rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: Versioned connection matrix must accompany new services or ports; role separation adds ownership review.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require explicit new-connection declaration and negative policy tests when adding a dependency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Same image and named-volume format permit reverting configuration; previous exposure returns on rollback.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Restore original memberships and remove only own policy tables; do not delete data volumes.

residualRisks: Allowed DB/service credentials can still be abused
Shared bootstrap may limit narrowing without code changes
No defense against kernel escape is proven

opportunities.recommendation: Choose Option2 for this local lab under balanced complexity; choose Option3 when parser-RCE isolation from API/admin is a hard requirement.

connectionPolicy.basis: configuration and read-only runtime snapshot; not enforced or exhaustively traffic-profiled
connectionPolicy.default: deny new peer, reverse and unapproved external connections
connectionPolicy.roleSplitException: API/ingestor -> reports-only HTTP relay -> admin9381; not a blanket allow to admin

openQuestions: Prove bridge/inet filter capability and persistence in current rootless namespace
Profile ClickHouse/DNS and per-role bootstrap under representative load
Select future model endpoints and egress ownership
Determine whether role separation resource/operations costs are justified
